name: Rekall
description: Rekall is a controlled memory-enhancement compound that temporarily supercharges episodic memory encoding and retrieval, allowing users to experience and re-access memories with extraordinary vividness and detail. Originally developed as a therapeutic for trauma processing and witness testimony enhancement, Nightshade's gray-market distribution channels have made it widely available for less sanctioned uses — corporate espionage, alibi construction, and the simple human desire to relive.
effects: Vivid, high-fidelity encoding of experiences during the active window
Enhanced retrieval of recent memories with sensory detail intact
Ability to 're-enter' specific memories with near-experiential clarity
Useful for witness recall, depositions, and forensic self-reporting
BCI-compatible: encoded memories can be partially exported as experiential data
side_effects: Memory reconsolidation vulnerability — retrieved memories become temporarily malleable and can be altered by suggestion or new information
Difficulty distinguishing between highly-encoded Rekall memories and imagination during off-dose periods
Emotional overwhelm when reliving traumatic or highly charged memories
Intrusive re-experiencing of encoded memories during sleep
Rare: memory sourcing failure — users lose track of which memories are Rekall-enhanced and which are baseline, eroding trust in their own episodic history
duration: Encoding window: 3-4 hours; retrieval enhancement: 6-8 hours
cultural_context: Rekall is the drug of grief, nostalgia, and crime. On the Shelf, it is used by people who want to relive the best moments of lives that have very few of them — a mother reliving the day her child was born, a veteran reliving the last time they felt part of something. It is also used by fixers and operatives who need to reconstruct events with precision, and by lawyers and investigators with flexible ethics who need witnesses to remember things with conviction. The reconsolidation vulnerability is the drug's most dangerous and most exploited feature — a Rekall-dosed subject recalling an event in the presence of someone who subtly reframes it will incorporate those changes into their permanent memory.
story_hooks: A key witness in a major corporate trial has been secretly dosed with Rekall and then had their memory of the incriminating event reconstructed — they now genuinely remember something that didn't happen, with total conviction, and there's no way to tell them the truth without understanding exactly what was done to them.

A Shelf resident has been using Rekall to relive a single day — the last day before something terrible — for so long that the reconstructed memory has diverged significantly from what actually happened, and they've begun to act on the false version.

A fixer discovers that someone has been dosing them periodically and sitting with them while they recall recent jobs — their operational memory has been systematically harvested and possibly altered, and they don't know what information they've given up or what memories they can no longer trust.
